svg.aria-label: How to write ಂ: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ಂ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಂ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Chimple (Sutara Learning Foundation, Bangalore), LIDO tracing lessons LIDO_kn4800 to LIDO_kn4806, chimple/chimple-zips at commit 5b137ab1 (October 2026): the hidden, ordered tracing paths for 34 consonants with ಂ, among them ಕಂ (trace image file-2g6kdrwp.svg) <https://github.com/chimple/chimple-zips/blob/5b137ab1bbd8516f9b4813f23c0e8e9c99f26156/LIDO_kn4800.zip>. Source note on variation: In all 34 of Chimple's consonant + anusvara trace images the ring is one path, drawn last, after the consonant's body and its talakattu, and in all 34 it runs anticlockwise; it starts at its left side (9 o'clock) in 20, at the top in 13 and at 11 o'clock in 1, so the path starts at the left. Chimple's recorded ಅಂ trace (chimple/bahama at commit 62608a6, assets/courses/kn/kn/res/paths, MPL-2.0) agrees: the ring is the second and last stroke and runs anticlockwise, starting at the top. The two repositories come from one organisation, so they are one source, not two. chimple-zips has no licence, so only facts are cited (order, start, direction, count); no path or artwork is copied. This is designer-authored and recorded teaching material, not a native-writer statistic, so confidence is medium; the Malayalam anusvara, which Moag draws clockwise, is a different sign in a different script. The bundle LIDO_kn4800.zip has sha256 af6c85b8683ee1cb.... The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline of the sign on its own.
